result.title: Temporary Routes and Building Access
result.objective: Learners will understand and correctly use remain in effect and step-free access in workplace notices.

exercises.prompt: In sentence s3, what does remain in effect mean when the diversion will remain in effect until inspectors confirm the road is safe?

options.text: The diversion will continue to be active until inspectors change it.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches continuing to be valid until changed.

options.text: The diversion will stop immediately and will not wait for inspectors.
options.explanation: Wrong because it describes immediate cancellation instead of continuation.

options.text: The diversion will be planned again only after inspectors leave the city.
options.explanation: Wrong because it describes future replanning instead of staying active.

exercises.explanation: The diversion stays active until inspectors confirm safety.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence using remain in effect.

options.text: The temporary safety rules will remain in effect until the manager updates them.
options.explanation: Correct because the verb form and time clause are natural.

options.text: The temporary safety rules will remains in effect until the manager updates them.
options.explanation: Wrong because remains should be remain after will.

options.text: The temporary safety rules will remain in effect to the manager updates them.
options.explanation: Wrong because to should be until before a clause.

exercises.explanation: Only the correct sentence uses the phrase with natural grammar.

exercises.prompt: In sentence s6, what does step-free access mean when passengers who need step-free access should check the updated stop map?

options.text: It means passengers can get free tickets without waiting in a line.
options.explanation: Wrong because it confuses free with no cost instead of no steps.

options.text: It means passengers can enter and move through the stops without using steps.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches moving without steps or stairs.

options.text: It means passengers must use stairs to reach the platform more quickly.
options.explanation: Wrong because it describes the opposite action of using stairs.

exercises.explanation: The phrase refers to moving without steps or stairs.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence using step-free access.

options.text: The office offers a step-free access to visitors in wheelchairs.
options.explanation: Wrong because a should be removed before the uncountable phrase.

options.text: The office offers step-free access to visitors in wheelchairs.
options.explanation: Correct because grammar and collocation are natural.

options.text: The office offers step-free access to visitors on wheelchairs.
options.explanation: Wrong because on should be in in the fixed phrase in wheelchairs.

exercises.explanation: Only one sentence uses the noun phrase with correct grammar.

exercises.prompt: You are an office assistant welcoming a job candidate for an interview. Write 2-3 sentences to tell the candidate how to enter the building comfortably. Use the phrase step-free access.
exercises.sampleAnswer: We look forward to meeting you tomorrow. Our main entrance offers step-free access, so you can reach reception without using stairs. Please let us know if you need any extra help.
selfCheck: I used the phrase step-free access correctly.
I describe entering without steps and offer help.
exercises.explanation: Compare with the model and self-assess; no automatic grade.
